name: Invention Disclosure Form
aliases: turn my notes into an invention disclosure
collect information for a patent application
help me describe my invention before filing
description: A structured pre-filing invention disclosure form capturing technical concepts, components, operation, essential/optional features, technical effects, development status, potential inventors, contribution evidence, and disclosure history. Acts as the foundational intake layer for downstream patent workflows.
jurisdiction_notes: Internal pre-filing intake workflow. Does not itself constitute a patent application, legal novelty assessment, patentability opinion, or binding inventorship determination. Governed by evidence capture best practices to feed US, EP, PCT, and national patent filings.

sections.heading: 1. Invention Title
sections.description: Descriptive title of the invention.

sections.heading: 2. Internal Project / Matter
sections.description: Internal project code, matter ID, or business unit.

sections.heading: 3. Technical Field
sections.description: General technological field and domain classification.

sections.heading: 4. Problem / Need
sections.description: The specific problem, challenge, or technical bottleneck addressed.

sections.heading: 5. Existing Approaches
sections.description: How the problem is currently addressed and shortcomings of those methods.

sections.heading: 6. Core Inventive Concept
sections.description: The central innovative insight, mechanism, or principle.

sections.heading: 7. Technical Description
sections.description: Detailed description of how the invention is structured and implemented.

sections.heading: 8. Components / Method Steps
sections.description: Detailed breakdown of structural elements or procedural steps.

sections.heading: 9. Operation
sections.description: How the components interact and operate in practice.

sections.heading: 10. Essential Features
sections.description: Features without which the core invention cannot function.

sections.heading: 11. Preferred Features
sections.description: Preferred embodiments providing optimal performance.

sections.heading: 12. Optional Features
sections.description: Non-essential enhancements, accessories, or fallback elements.

sections.heading: 13. Alternative Embodiments
sections.description: Alternative structural, algorithmic, or operational configurations.

sections.heading: 14. Technical Effects / Advantages
sections.description: Observed or expected technical benefits achieved over known approaches.

sections.heading: 15. Examples / Test Results
sections.description: Experimental data, bench test measurements, or simulation results.

sections.heading: 16. Development / Prototype Status
sections.description: Current readiness: Concept, Design, Prototype, Tested, or Pilot.

sections.heading: 17. Known Limitations
sections.description: Operating boundaries, known failure modes, or environmental constraints.

sections.heading: 18. Commercial Embodiment
sections.description: Intended product release, customer use case, or service integration.

sections.heading: 19. Known Design-Arounds
sections.description: How a competitor might attempt to bypass the primary solution.

sections.heading: 20. Known Prior Art / References
sections.description: Relevant patents, academic papers, commercial products, or standards.

sections.heading: 21. Potential Inventors
sections.description: Individuals who contributed to the conception of inventive features.

sections.heading: 22. Contribution Matrix
sections.description: Mapping of each individual's technical contribution to inventive features.

sections.heading: 23. Ownership / Collaboration Context
sections.description: Employment relationships, university ties, contractor agreements, and grants.

sections.heading: 24. Public / External Disclosure History
sections.description: Timeline of publications, presentations, sales, NDA sharings, or disclosures.

sections.heading: 25. Earlier Patent Filings
sections.description: Existing provisional, PCT, or foreign filings relating to this subject matter.

sections.heading: 26. Supporting Documents
sections.description: Attached specifications, test reports, CAD files, or source notes.

sections.heading: 27. Drawing Needs
sections.description: Identified figures, flowcharts, or system diagrams needed for patent drafting.

sections.heading: 28. Open Questions
sections.description: Technical or legal gaps to be resolved before patent filing.

sections.heading: 29. Review Flags
sections.description: Identified legal flags: inventorship, disclosure, ownership, or specialist review.

sections.heading: 30. Provenance Summary
sections.description: Audit record of source documents, user inputs, and verification states.
